correctness.rationale: Write Q=q^n. Each x≠0 is an idempotent with probability 1/(Q−1) by transitivity on nonzero vectors. Distinct collinear vectors x and tx cannot both work, since then t²=t with t≠0,1. Among the (Q−1)(Q−q) ordered independent pairs, exactly those with dependent coordinatewise squares must be discarded; each remaining pair has joint probability 1/((Q−1)(Q−q)). With mean one this factorial moment is the variance. In characteristic two, squaring is an automorphism and preserves independence. In odd characteristic, for x with r nonzero coordinates, a proportional squared y has (q−1)/2 possible square ratios and 2^r sign patterns per ratio; exactly two patterns give collinear y. Summing binomially over support sizes gives (q−1)((2q−1)^n−2q^n+1)/2 excluded pairs. The r=2 term gives strict positivity of the defect, its expansion gives (2^(n−1)−1)q^(1−n)+O_n(q^(−n)), and n=1 gives the unique nonzero solution x=M^(-1). Independently looping over determinant-nonzero 2×2 matrices and counting solutions among nonzero pairs gives histograms 0:16, 1:20, 2:8, 3:4 over F3 and 0:60, 1:90, 3:30 over F4 (replay with F2[t]/(t²+t+1)), confirming 5/6 and 1. Inspected frozen verification notes and script without executing the uploaded script; the proof covers the universal claim, not the finite checks.

value.rationale: The uniform invertible ensemble and the second factorial moment are motivated by an existing fixed-point prediction. The exact finite-field correction isolates an odd-characteristic obstruction due to square-map projective collisions, distinguishes finite from limiting behavior, and gives the size of the discrepancy uniformly in dimension and field size. This is useful independently of a full distribution and is not a recomputation of the known mean or characteristic-two law.
